s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic skin lesions with slow growth, associated with venous insufficiency and neurological deficits
salient_findings: Bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
key_facts: Female patient in her early 50s
Multiple skin lesions on the lower legs
Lesions have been growing slowly since age 24
Lesions bleed occasionally after trauma
Patient uses a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia
History of intracranial hemorrhage
Recurrent seizures at age 4
Lipolymphedema of the lower legs
Family history of similar conditions
Father died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography showed intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations
Histopathology revealed hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and dilated venous-like malformations
Genetic testing detected a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

shortlist.label: Cerebral cavernous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: KRIT1 variant detected, matches family history of intracranial hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions, venous insufficiency, and lipolymphedema match syndrome characteristics

shortlist.label: Venous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Sonography and histopathology confirm presence of venous malformations

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Neurological deficits and skin lesions are consistent with this syndrome

shortlist.label: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
shortlist.why_kept: Family history and presence of vascular malformations make this a plausible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, which is a known cause of cerebral cavernous malformations, along with the patient's history of intracranial hemorrhage and family history of similar conditions, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has vascular malformations and lipolymphedema, the presence of a KRIT1 variant and the specific type of malformations are more consistent with cerebral cavernous malformation.

rejected.label: Venous malformation
rejected.why: The diagnosis is too narrow and does not account for the patient's neurological history or the genetic findings.

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's presentation does not include the characteristic port-wine stain of Sturge-Weber syndrome, and the genetic findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and genetic findings do not align with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, which typically involves telangiectasias and is associated with different genetic mutations.
